standard_prerequisites.name: Cut rule
standard_prerequisites.statement: From derivations of Gamma_0 sequent A and of A, Gamma_1 sequent (empty right side) one derives Gamma_0, Gamma_1 sequent (empty).
standard_prerequisites.use: The displayed derivation cuts pi_0 ( Gamma_0 sequent A ) against pi_1 ( A, Gamma_1 sequent empty ).

standard_prerequisites.name: Inconsistency via derivable empty sequent
standard_prerequisites.statement: Gamma is inconsistent iff some finite Gamma' subseteq Gamma has Gamma' sequent (empty right side) derivable in LK.
standard_prerequisites.use: The cut conclusion Gamma_0, Gamma_1 sequent (empty) with Gamma_0, Gamma_1 subseteq Gamma witnesses the inconsistency.

core_obligations: Statement (prop at 873): if Gamma proves A and Gamma cup {A} is inconsistent, then Gamma is inconsistent.

Construction (proof from 876): take finite Gamma_0, Gamma_1 subseteq Gamma with LK-derivations pi_0 of Gamma_0 sequent A and pi_1 of A, Gamma_1 sequent (empty); display one prooftree cutting pi_0 over pi_1 to obtain Gamma_0, Gamma_1 sequent (empty).
Conclusion: Gamma_0 cup Gamma_1 subseteq Gamma, hence Gamma is inconsistent.
proof_roadmap: Unpack both hypotheses into finite witnesses with derivations pi_0 and pi_1.
Cut pi_0 over pi_1 to derive the empty sequent from Gamma_0, Gamma_1.
Conclude inconsistency of Gamma by the finite-subset criterion.
difficulty_reason: Provability-to-inconsistency propagation (statement 873-876, proof 878-896): the cut-composition derivation carried in span; substantive step is cutting the derivation of A against the derivation of the empty sequent from A. H2.
